articles.title: Uganda Communist League members arrested after inaugural congress
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content: Members of the newly formed Communist League of Uganda were arrested and allegedly subjected to severe treatment by state security forces days after the organization concluded its inaugural National Congress, according to a statement issued by the League. The Communist League of Uganda said several of its members, including Vice Chairperson Habibu Twahala, Odeke Dan, and Namususwa Patricia, were arrested on August 29, 2026, while participating in a mobilization drive. The arrests came shortly after the League held its first National Congress, marking the organization’s formal effort to establish itself as a political organization representing working-class interests in Uganda. According to the League, however, its members were targeted for engaging in political mobilization. Their “crime,” the organization said, was “nothing more than standing up, in public, for the dignity of the working people of Uganda.” “For this, they were seized, detained, and held against their will by a state apparatus that fears the organized power of its own people,” the League said. Allegations of mistreatment The League alleges that the arrested members were severely beaten while in detention. Those involved in securing their release said they remained concerned about their physical condition, with the detainees reportedly not feeling well following their treatment in custody. The League said the detained members were eventually released following pressure and mobilization from supporters in Uganda and abroad. “We are relieved to report that, following sustained pressure, mobilization, and the unrelenting demands of comrades both at home and abroad, all those detained have now been released,” the statement said. But the organization insists that it did not regard the release as an end to the matter. “But their freedom was not given, it was extracted, bitterly and only after our collective refusal to remain silent,” the League said. League calls out wider repression The Communist League of Uganda said the arrests should be understood within a wider political context. “This arrest did not occur in a vacuum,” the League said. “It is part of a broader pattern of state repression against organizers, trade unionists, and left political movements across Uganda who dare to challenge entrenched power, corruption, and the economic order that keeps the majority of our people in poverty while a small elite enriches itself.” The organization argued that the criminalization of political mobilization was directly connected to the ability of working people to organize collectively. “Mass mobilization is criminalized precisely because it is effective, because when working people organize and raise their voices together, they threaten the interests that depend on their silence and division,” it said. The League further said that the arrests represented an attempt to discourage political organizing beyond the individuals detained. “The targeting of Comrades Twahala, Odeke, and Namususwa is an attack not just on three individuals, but on the right of all Ugandans to organize, assemble, and demand a better future,” the statement said. “It is an attempt to instill fear in our ranks and to deter others from joining the struggle. We say clearly it will not work.” Calls for political freedoms Following the arrests, the Communist League of Uganda demanded an end to what it described as harassment and surveillance of its members and other activists involved in peaceful political organizing. Read more: Uganda’s largest non-state media group under military siege The League called for guarantees of the constitutional rights to freedom of assembly, expression and political association for all Ugandan citizens. It also demanded that any remaining charges or conditions imposed on the released members be dropped. The organization appealed to communist, socialist and progressive organizations internationally to publicize what it described as an act of repression. “We call upon fraternal communist, socialist, and progressive organizations across the world to publicize this act of repression through your own networks, publications, and platforms,” the statement said. The Communist Party Marxist of Kenya also expressed solidarity with the Communist League of Uganda and called for the release of its members. Arrests follow inaugural congress Notably, the arrests came immediately after the Communist League of Uganda’s inaugural National Congress, at a moment when the organization is attempting to consolidate its structures and expand its political work. The emergence of the League adds another left-wing organization to Uganda’s contested political realities, where opposition politicians, activists, trade unionists and civil society groups have raised concerns over restrictions on political organizing and public assembly. The political environment has also included the continued detention of opposition figure Kizza Besigye, whose case has drawn international attention and renewed scrutiny of political freedoms in Uganda.

articles.title: Operation Southern Spear: uncovering the CIA’s killing spree in Latin America
articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content: A drone hovering over a burning Ecuadorian fishing boat hours after it was bombed belonged to a San Diego-based defense contractor with an $800 million contract with the US Navy. Investigative journalist Camila Lourdes Galarza tells Zoe Alexandra and Rania Khalek that boat was one of three unarmed fishing vessels bombed in what the Washington Post later confirmed was part of a covert CIA program to kill “suspected drug traffickers” in the Pacific – without any oversight or public acknowledgment. As Operation Southern Spear marks its first year, Galarza breaks down how Ecuadorian President and Miami-born billionaire Daniel Noboa has turned his country into a testing ground for US military expansion under Trump’s Donroe Doctrine: from former Blackwater mercenaries at polling stations, to martial law decrees shielding US troops from Ecuadorian law, to the SOUTHCOM general she says admitted the real target of all of this is Ecuador’s lithium stores and rare earth minerals. Galarza connects the boat strikes, on which she reported extensively for Drop Site News, to a much larger pattern, linking Fernando Cerimedo’s CIA and Israel ties to a US embassy plot to interfere in Colombia’s elections, to the assassination in June of Ecuadorian prosecutor Alexandra Bravo as US troops patrolled the streets. articles.title: US strikes hit wedding in Iran as death toll from latest strikes crosses 18
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content: At least 18 Iranians, including children, were killed and around 80 others were injured in the latest US airstrikes in southern Iran’s Khuzestan, Bushehr, Baluchestan, and Hormozgan provinces late on the night of Tuesday, September 1, IRNA reported. Several Iranian media reports claimed one of the sites attacked on Tuesday night was a wedding celebration in Sirik in the southern Hormozgan province. At least four people, including a four years old child, were killed and around 70 others were wounded in that attack. Meanwhile, Iran rejected the claims made by the US Central Command that the overnight attacks only targeted locations belonging to Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), in retaliation to attacks on commercial ships and US servicemen in the region. On Wednesday morning, Iran retaliated by striking US military outposts in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, and Iraq with drones and missiles. The IRGC also claimed it downed yet another US MQ-9 drone. The IRGC said its retaliatory attacks on Kuwait have “killed a number of enemy elements.” The latest round of military strikes and counter strikes in the over six-month-long war on Iran began on Sunday when US forces carried out attacks on Iran’s Larak island on Sunday, killing scores of Iranians. The military strikes on Larak Island were carried out after a weeks-long halt in military hostilities. The Trump administration in the US had previously claimed it would prioritize economically isolating Iran instead of carrying out further attacks. After Sunday’s strikes, US CENTCOM said the attacks were part of its efforts to prevent Iran from laying fresh mines in the Strait of Hormuz in the future. Iran ridiculed Washington’s claims, calling them a “fantasy” and retaliated by striking US military bases in Jordan and the UAE. In a statement issued late Tuesday night, the IRGC claimed that the “desperate” attacks carried out by the US would only tighten its grip on the Strait of Hormuz instead of weakening it in any way. The IRGC also claimed two oil tankers hit a mine and caught fire while trying to use the US-backed route to cross the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. At least two crew members were reported killed in the incident. The cycle of US atrocities Responding to the latest attacks on civilians in Iran, Esmail Baghaei, official spokesperson of its foreign ministry called it a completion of the “catalogue of atrocities” carried out by the US since the attack on school children in Minab on the first day of the war. More than 160 school children were killed in the strike in Minab on February 28. In a similar strike on the same day, 21 civilians were killed in Lamerd sports hall. Following the global outrage, the US initially denied the attacks and later dismissed them as “human errors,” refusing to hold those responsible accountable. The targeting of civilians during war is a war crime. “More dangerous than the bomb itself is the normalization of bombing; and more dangerous than silence is the conversion of silence into legitimacy,” Baghaei said, vowing a strong response to the attacks. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and head of its delegation negotiating peace terms, condemned the latest attacks on civilians. “If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it’s Satan,” Ghalibaf wrote in a post on X , comparing attacks on the wedding celebration with attacks in Minab and Lamerd sports hall. Over 3,500 Iranians, including its former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei and several other top military and political leaders, have been killed in the war started by the US and Israel. The war has also heavily impacted the global economy. The Strait of Hormuz, a major route for global trade in energy, has been blocked for months now causing a rise in global energy prices. International efforts to end the war have failed after the US refused to adhere to the norms of the peace agreement, called the Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June. Iran has recently reiterated that if the US agrees to adhere to all the provisions of the MoU the situation in the region would be resolved, which may include the normalization of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Unabated violence: 47 dead and 60 kidnapped in Haiti in August 24 massacre
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content: The violence in Haiti shows no signs of stopping. On August 24, 47 people were massacred in Kenscoff, near the capital, Port-au-Prince, according to the UN. Of the 47 people killed, 22 were murdered in a local church. According to authorities, the massacre took place amid a gang war for control of territories in the Caribbean nation. María Fernanda Arocha, an analyst with Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), told El País : “The latest attack in Kenscoff is yet another example of how gangs resort to large-scale killings of civilians to subdue the local population and impose their authority. The raid also serves as a stark reminder of the challenges the government faces in consolidating the results of its operations against the gangs.” UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the incident: “I condemn the latest gang attack on Kenscoff, a commune on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince, in Haiti, that reportedly killed at least 47 people, including 22 who were reportedly executed in a church compound where they had found shelter.” Guterres added : “The relentless gang attacks on communities & the loss of civilian lives underscore the alarming security conditions in Haiti & reinforce the urgent need to intensify Haitian & international security efforts to counter gangs. I reiterate my call for Haitian authorities to ensure that those responsible for such attacks are held accountable.” For several years now, a coalition of international forces, under a UN mandate, has been operating in the Caribbean country to help address a security crisis that seems to only be escalating, despite the promises made by foreign armed forces. According to some reports , only 1,000 of the coalition’s 5,000 troops are currently deployed, leading many to call for the plan to be carried out with all available troops. The leader who allegedly ordered the attack is also said to have ordered the kidnapping of nearly 60 people to prevent a strong response from the authorities, threatening to execute the hostages if his gang is attacked. According to reports, 13 people have already been released. In this regard, Pope Leo XIV demanded the immediate release of the hostages and called on the authorities to take action to halt the spiral of violence in Haiti: “I ask that the hostages be released without delay, and I issue a concerned appeal to all those in positions of responsibility to make concrete efforts to ensure the safety of the population and put an end to all forms of violence.” For his part, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé demanded a “firm response” from his soldiers and police: “The Kenscoff massacre will not go unpunished.” He also stated that specific operations are underway to dismantle criminal networks and regain control of the occupied areas, although these promises have yet to be fulfilled. Indeed, the severe security and economic crisis in Haiti, a country of 12 million people, shows no signs of abating. According to the UN , in 2026 alone, more than 3,000 people have been killed and more than 1,400 injuries have been reported. Added to this is the plight of more than 1 million internally displaced persons who have been forced to flee as a result of the violence. According to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), half the country requires some form of urgent humanitarian aid, which highlights the extremely severe scale of an internal war that shows no signs of abating. Only 30% of health care facilities are operational; the rest are unable to operate due to a lack of staff and security to care for patients. Added to this is sexual violence, which disproportionately affects women and girls: 700 people have reported some form of sexual violence. In addition, more than 100 cases of kidnapping have been reported, although several NGOs claim that the actual numbers are much higher – it’s just that not all cases are reported due to a lack of security guarantees.

articles.title: The USS Lincoln’s ‘leisure trip’ to Thailand: a port call of US neocolonialism and femicide
articles.author: Benyasiri Eimviriyapong
articles.content: The arrival of the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) for a “leisure trip” in Thailand before returning to its campaign of destruction against the people of West Asia demands immediate interrogation and opposition. For us Thai people, and those in sites of American plunder across the globe, this a rattling of the US’ cold war colonial chains on its most loyal lap dog, while conducting a war of aggression in Iran and the ongoing genocide in Palestine. In allowing the USS Lincoln to dock, the Thai ruling elites are once again facilitating a system of imperial violence that extends far beyond Southeast Asian borders, a system which in our case, is predicated on sexual violence and femicide. Thailand has a long history of being a colonial vassal of the US today a “major non-NATO ally” since 2003. While Thailand has sought to balance its relationships by pivoting toward China in recent years, the US continues to invest heavily in maintaining influence over Thai politics and military institutions, viewing the kingdom as strategically vital . The visit from the USS Lincoln is thus a confirmation of the ongoing alliance maintenance: an embarrassing reminder of the rulers of the Kingdom of Thailand’s bootlicking tendency to American military ambitions. This is a tendency not shared by the people of Thailand, in particular the country’s women, who have most suffered from US violence in the course of this relationship. It is the continuation of a long history of imperial violence, where women’s bodies have served as currency for Thailand’s relations with the west. The USS Lincoln will arrive in the port in the eastern seaboard of Thailand which was established as the primary American staging post and Rest & Relaxation site of its assault on Vietnam from the 60s to 70s. Today, the city of Pattaya is perhaps the largest site of sex tourism, of imperial rape, in the world, thanks entirely to its history of accommodating the American GI. The war machine docks itself to the structural legacy of American neocolonialism, a legacy of plundering Thailand into a site of sexual exploitation, and a legacy of femicide, where the state and capital work hand in hand to systematically render women’s lives as expendable in the name of profit and US geopolitical hegemony. The myth of Thailand’s sovereignty Official Thai histories celebrate the kingdom as a rare Southeast Asian nation that has managed to escape the claws of European colonization through the diplomatic acumen of our brilliant monarchs. However, this narrative obscures the people’s reality. As early Marxist Thai historians recognized, Thailand was a “semi-colonial” state , beginning with the Bowring Treaty of 1855, which granted extraterritoriality to British subjects and monopolized trade into colonial hands. The treaty, signed under gunboat diplomacy – akin the the Unequal Treaties with China, rendered Siam a de-facto buffer state between British and French colonial interests, making it sovereign only in name. “Thailand is the US’ 51st state “ The departure of European powers did not bring genuine independence but replaced one master with another. Following World War II, the United States assumed the role of an imperial patron, viewing Thailand as an essential bulwark against “ communist aggression ” in Southeast Asia. From 1950 onwards, successive Thai military fascist dictatorships, beginning with Sarit Thanarat’s 1957 coup, orchestrated with the US support, came to heel at the governing call of Washington. The US poured over $1.5 billion in military and economic aid into the country, embedding a system of dependency to American interests within the Thai military, while Thailand hosted seven US air force bases and hundreds of thousands of troops – primarily for Rest & Relaxation – during the American war of aggression in Vietnam. In reality, Thailand was colonized not through direct territorial seizure but through economic domination, military presence, and political subservience – through a complex network of financial geopolitical mechanisms. As the Tricontinental put it back in 1969 : “Without a doubt, Thailand is one of the most faithful in carrying out orders from Washington. Therefore there is no doubt that Marshal Kittikachorn (Thanon) was completely sincere when he stated that the United States could consider Thailand the 51st state.” The US military’s Prostitution Industrial Complex The war of aggression in Vietnam has transformed Thailand into the US military’s primary Rest and Recreation R&R hub. Soldiers on leave after murdering Vietnamese people and drowning the country in Agent Orange would be flown to Thai bases where the patriarchal violence and femicide were institutionalized as both reward and necessity. Sarit’s military state, for example, actively engineered this as a matter of national policy . In 1959, even before the major troop buildups, a group of 500 US soldiers were transported from their base in Nakhon Ratchasima, to – what was then – the small fishing village of Pattaya, Chonburi, a trip facilitated by local authorities and effectively marking the village as a designated site for their R&R. This was formalized in 1964 when the Thai and US governments signed an official agreement to provide R&R facilities for GIs, a pact that transformed Pattaya and other areas into sprawling “entertainment” complexes. Between 1964 and 1976, approximately 700,000 international soldiers arrived annually for week-long stays during the US assault on Indochina. Thai women’s bodies were transformed into national resources, exploited to attract foreign currency and fuel economic development. Cynthia Enloe writes in Bananas, Beaches and Bases (1990) this is the logic of imperialism, capitalism, and patriarchy: the female body becomes an instrument for capital accumulation, and the state facilitates this extraction. Thailand’s sex industry constitutes a public, institutionalized system of exploitation legitimized by the state and fueled by international, particularly US, demand for a constant supply of women’s labor. Both unpaid (reproductive) labor like cleaners, cooks, maids, etc. as well as hyper-exploitative sexual labor. Today, the city of Pattaya has been transformed into permanent zones of sexual commerce, serving international sex tourism for men beyond military personnel. Through an economic lens: American GIs created a demand that incentivized sex “entrepreneurs” (pimps and traffickers) to “professionalize” their activities. After the US military base in Chonburi was evicted in 1975 (thanks to the brave work of militant leftist organizers – students, farmers, and the working class of Thailand) these districts retained the infrastructure and reputation that attracted sex tourists, perpetuating a vicious cycle. The entire area surrounding the former bases now feature luxury beach front hotels, all marketed to foreigners, and as we see in the case of the USS Lincoln, still host western imperialist military, as a site to pimp out our women. Class collaborators like Pattaya Mayor Poramet Ngampichet said the city is ready to welcome US military personnel seeking to rest and spend time in the resort city after their lengthy deployment of aggression. Across Southeast Asia, fluctuations in sexual violence went hand in hand with US military presence. It was always an orchestrated industry of sexual supply chains meeting military demand. In the end, it is the women who bear the rawest brunt of this imperial patriarchal violence. The same conditions that allowed networks like Epsteins to operate : the vulnerability of victims, the complicity of power structures, and the commodification of women’s bodies, are mirrored in the structural conditions that have made Thailand a global destination for sexual exploitation. Femicide: the ultimate outcome of structural gender violence Femicide extends beyond individual acts of murder to encompass all structural conditions that render women’s lives disposable, diminish their life opportunities, and subject them to systemic violence. The system where women are systematically wrapped into sex work due to existing infrastructure and poverty, where the state facilitates and profits from our exploitation, where US military presence created the demand, and where Western tourism perpetuates supply – this is femicide. It is the systematic sacrifice of women’s physical and psychological integrity, autonomy, and our very lives, for imperialist ends. Thailand’s women are being exploited, not only for the profit of sex tourism, but also to sustain the geopolitical alliance that makes Thailand a staging ground for imperial wars. The political stability that the US seeks to maintain in Thailand depends in part on the economic conditions that continue to entrench women in sexual exploitation. These systems of political maintenance include anti-communist death squads, maintaining dependent military ties , prohibiting economic sovereignty , and ensuring a staunchly anti communist leadership . As long as tourism-dependent economies require the continued flow of foreign patriarchal consumers, and as long as the state prioritizes capital accumulation over women’s right to life, Thailand’s women will bear the human cost of the US-Thailand alliance. The lasting culture of hypersexualization On social media, the arrival of 5,000 US soldiers in Thailand is being treated as a comical punchline for Americans.This reveals how deeply the hypersexualization of Thailand’s women and the systemic exploitation of our bodies have been normalized in the male consciousness. Some comments include “Big pay day for those girl[s], might find their husband,” “Tons of Gallons of Semen incoming,” and “Straight to Bangcock; all soldiers are sexcited about sexercises.” These statements are the amalgamation of attitudes left behind by American GIs. These sentiments are a direct descendant of the American culture that has portrayed Asian women as hypersexual and submissive since the era of US military aggression in the region. The exploitation of Thailand’s women is considered entertaining an outcome of a military port call. The existence and perpetuation of this culture reveals the neo-colonial system that has systematically commodified women for the pleasure and profit of the empire. The USS Lincoln is a continuation The USS Lincoln’s arrival in Thailand is just the latest iteration of a relationship forged through imperial domination and sustained by the systematic exploitation of Thailand’s women. The US actively and consciously created and shaped the sexual violence economy that now persists as a permanent feature of the Thai socio-economic system. When the ship docks, it is enjoying the fruits of its Cold War victory, marking the continuity of the ongoing structural femicide enabled by Thai-American relations. We must see the women in Pattaya, in Nakhon Ratchasima, in Nakhon Phanom, in Takhli, in Ubon Ratchathani, in Udon Thani, and across Thailand as individuals caught in an oppressive web of global capitalism, imperial legacy, and the crudest form of patriarchal violence. The solution is not Western-led anti-trafficking interventions that further disempower Thai women, but a revolutionary overhaul of the economic and political arrangements that made our exploitation profitable in the first place. The USS Lincoln’s visit ought to be met with the most extreme opposition, from the history it represents to the future it portends. Until the structural conditions that produce sexual exploitation are dismantled, every port call is an act of violence on our lands and bodies. Benyasiri Eimviriyapong is an editor, translator, and propagandist at Dindeng , a journal and publishing collective which seeks to decode the semi-feudal, the semi-capitalist, and the semi-colonial of Thailand. Her professional focus is on ecology, state power, and the application of revolutionary feminist politics in daily life. This article was produced by Globetrotter .

articles.title: Why the US just branded Palestine Action ‘global terrorists’ | w/ Asa Winstanley
articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content: A Palestine solidarity org that disbanded itself more than a year ago just got labeled a “global terrorist organization” by the US. Asa Winstanley tells Rania Khalek and Zoe Alexandra Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s designation announced last week was never really about Palestine Action, which never posed a threat even when it existed — it’s about Israel. The investigative journalist with Electronic Intifada recalls Marco Rubio’s July conference on “transnational far-left terrorism” was attended by Israel, which had already pushed the UK to ban the group last year. So with no organization left to fund and no operations to disrupt, why sanction a group that’s already gone? Winstanley explains Palestine Action’s nonviolent campaign — shutting down four sites belonging to Elbit Systems, Israel’s largest private arms firm, including its drone factories — proved so effective that Britain’s Labour government, deeply beholden to the pro-Israel lobby under Keir Starmer, rushed to outlaw it entirely. The ban placed Palestine Action in the same legal category as the Islamic State and Al Qaeda under the Terrorism Act — a deliberate choice Winstanley says is part of a broader pattern of weaponizing antisemitism to silence Palestine solidarity on both sides of the Atlantic. articles.title: “Went to Sea and Never Came Back”: Families of Fishermen Seek Answers After Deadly U.S. Boat Strikes
articles.content: A year ago today, the United States bombed a small boat in the Caribbean, killing nine people on board. Two survivors clung to the wreckage for 45 minutes, reportedly waving for help, before a second “double-tap” strike killed them, too. President Trump posted a video of the first attack on social media, announcing that 11 terrorists had been killed in a military operation that would be called “Operation Southern Spear.” The second video, showing the killing of the survivors, has never been released. The bombings have continued for a year, killing at least 227 people in nearly 70 separate strikes. The Pentagon often accuses the boats it targets of narcotrafficking. In a new documentary, the investigative team at Al Jazeera’s Fault Lines traveled to St. Lucia and Colombia to speak with two families who believe their loved ones, both fishermen, were killed at sea by U.S. airstrikes. “They describe it as a war. They describe these people as enemy combatants that are attacking America,” says Josh Rushing, a senior correspondent for Fault Lines who worked on the documentary. In reality, “it’s unclear, really, if the U.S. government knows who they’re killing … They’ve never named anyone in any of the strikes.” “We had the 'war on drugs,' the 'war on terror.' This is kind of the worst of both,” says Rushing.

articles.title: “Stand Up for Multifaith Democracy”: U.S. Activists, Lawmakers Protest India’s RSS & Hindu Supremacy
articles.content: Demonstrators gathered outside Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday to protest against the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, a far-right Indian paramilitary Hindu nationalist organization with close ties to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The leader of the RSS , Mohan Bhagwat, was holding a rally inside the arena to launch a global speaking tour marking the 100th anniversary of the RSS . The RSS’s “explicitly stated mission, its purpose, is to create a Hindu Rashtra, a Hindu nation — to take the India that is a secular and inclusive democracy and transform it into a country that is just for Hindus, where Muslims, Christians, Sikhs and other minorities are basically erased,” says Sunita Vishwanath, co-founder of Hindus for Human Rights Action. ” RSS affiliates, these Hindu right-wing organizations, exist in growing numbers in the diaspora, especially in America.” “In 1939, [Madison Square Garden] hosted a Nazi rally with swastikas hung from the banners around a portrait of George Washington. They said they wouldn’t do something like that again, and yet here they were hosting Mohan Bhagwat, spouting a similar fascist ideology,” says Brad Lander, a Democratic nominee for Congress from New York City, who joined Saturday’s protest.

articles.author: Scot Nakagawa
articles.content: The far-right’s assault on democracy has always run through the bodies, agency, and political power of women. That’s not incidental, it’s structural. In this episode, Scot sits down with Tamika Middleton, Chief Strategy Officer of the Women’s March and co-founder of Kindred Southern Healing Justice Collective, to talk about what it means to organize at the intersection of mass action and healing… Source

articles.title: ‘They destroy, we build’: Gazans rebuild their homes out of mud and rubble
articles.author: Tareq S. Hajjaj
articles.content: As Israel continues to prevent the entry of reconstruction materials into Gaza, Palestinians rebuild their homes with salvaged rebar, recovered limestone, and clay. “This is the evidence of our love for our land,” Fayez Abu Shamala tells Mondoweiss.
